# Synthetic compatibility and authenticator fixtures

These files contain only deliberately synthetic test material. The P-256 private
key in `go-passkey.json` is scalar **1**, a public test vector, and must never be
used by a real account or deployment. No personal credentials were exported.

`go-compat.json` was generated by Go 1.27.1 with
`go run tests/fixtures/generate-go-compat.go`. The generator uses the same
standard-library AES-256-GCM nonce-prefix/AAD, HMAC purpose and base64 encodings
as baseline `6fc5145a7f0983dd1a3c92a44216ec9de041df55`. It records independently
computed ciphertext/plaintext and CSRF expected outputs. The Rust tests read
checked-in JSON; Go is not needed for normal tests or CI.

`go-passkey.json` was serialized by the actual baseline dependency,
`github.com/go-webauthn/webauthn v0.18.2`, using the baseline's Go module files.
It contains a valid EC2/ES256 COSE public key, synthetic PKCS#8 test key, original
Go credential/attestation JSON, and original `webauthn.SessionData` JSON. It is
not produced by the Rust adapter. `go-password.json` uses the same baseline
module with `golang.org/x/crypto/argon2` and a fixed synthetic salt; its PHC hash
is verified by Rust without rehashing it first. Regenerate it with
`go-baseline/password.go` using the same temporary module procedure. To regenerate, make a temporary directory,
export the baseline `go.mod` and `go.sum` there with `git show`, then run the
absolute path to `go-baseline/generate.go` from that temporary directory. For
example, with the paths adjusted to the checkout:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/foltivo-go-vector
git show 6fc5145a7f0983dd1a3c92a44216ec9de041df55:go.mod > /tmp/foltivo-go-vector/go.mod
git show 6fc5145a7f0983dd1a3c92a44216ec9de041df55:go.sum > /tmp/foltivo-go-vector/go.sum
cd /tmp/foltivo-go-vector
go run /absolute/checkout/tests/fixtures/go-baseline/generate.go
```

Review/diff the generated output before replacing the checked-in JSON. The Rust
legacy tests substitute only the test account's UUID string bytes, origin,
current challenge/algorithm list when finishing an in-flight registration, and
the PostgreSQL ceremony expiry. The credential public data and Go-only metadata
remain the Go-produced vector. Successful assertions update the hybrid record;
tests check preserved attestation/public key and advancing counters.

`authenticator.mjs` drives the maintained
[Chromium DevTools WebAuthn domain](https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/WebAuthn/)
through its debugging pipe. It starts an isolated ephemeral browser profile and
loopback origin and creates a CTAP2 authenticator with resident keys and user
verification. It uses the browser's real `navigator.credentials.create/get`
implementation and signed responses. The application retains its actual
signature, UV, origin, challenge, user-handle and counter checks. Negative UV/UP
cases use Chromium's explicit response-override testing controls; they do not
change the server verifier.

The adapter accepts JSON lines over stdin and returns JSON lines on stdout.
It never connects to a live identity provider or frontend. The Cargo fixture
owns its process group, applies startup/reply/shutdown timeouts and terminates
owned browser processes on failure. Browser profiles and local HTTP servers are
removed at normal shutdown; abrupt host termination can leave temporary files.
